hero.title: Constructors
intro.0: You have written methods that take a value and hand one back. An object needs the same thing at the moment it is born: someone has to say which cat this is. That job belongs to a constructor - the code that runs once, when the object is made, to set up what it starts with. Here you write a few, and watch where the values you pass in actually end up.
task.1.title: Set the object up as it is made
task.1.context: A `class` says what a cat has; it does not say which cat. Without a constructor, `new Cat()` gives you a cat with an empty name - every one identical. A constructor closes that gap. It carries the class's own name, takes the values the caller has to supply, and hands nothing back - not even `void`, because it is not answering a question. It runs once, at `new`, and then it is over.
task.1.goal.1: Store what was handed in, so `Name()` returns `Ana`.
task.2.title: Each object keeps its own
task.2.context: One `new` makes one object, so the constructor runs once per cat - twice here, with a different name each time. The two cats share the class and nothing else: the field `_name` is not one box that both write into, it is one box inside each of them. That is the whole reason a class is worth writing. Describe a cat once, then make as many as you need.
task.2.goal.0: Build a second cat called `Katya`, alongside `Ana`.
task.2.goal.1: Print both names - each cat answers with its own.
task.3.title: Two values, in order
task.3.context: A constructor takes as many parameters as the object needs to start. The `parameter` is the slot you write in the declaration - `string name`, `int age`. The `argument` is the value at the call - `"Ana"`, `8`. They are matched by position, not by name. Swap the two at this call and the compiler stops you, because the types differ - it will not always be so kind.
task.3.goal.0: Store both values, each in its own field.
task.4.title: What it keeps, what it is handed
task.4.concept: Fields outlive a call; parameters do not
task.4.context: `Report` compares two numbers that reach it in different ways. `_hoursSinceMeal` was set at `new` and belongs to the cat - it is still there between calls, and each cat has its own. `hoursUntilHungry` arrives when the call starts and is gone when it ends; the next call gets a fresh one. Same look on the page, different lifetimes - a parameter is a local variable that happened to be filled in by the caller.
task.4.goal.0: Decide with `_hoursSinceMeal` and the `hoursUntilHungry` handed in.
task.4.goal.1: Return the name, then ` hungry` or ` fed`.
task.5.title: Work it out once, at the start
task.5.concept: A constructor can do more than copy
task.5.context: So far each constructor has copied its parameters straight into fields, but it does not have to. Anything the object should be true of from the moment it exists can be settled here - and settled once, rather than recomputed by every method that asks. Note `SpacePerCat`: the rule has a name, so the number 2 is not scattered across the file waiting to disagree with itself.
task.5.goal.0: Work out the space needed in the constructor and keep it.
concept.pr-constructor.def: The code that runs once when an object is made, to set up what it starts with. It carries the class's own name and hands nothing back.
card.title: Constructors
card.blurb: An object has to start somewhere. Write the code that runs when it is made, hand it the values it needs, and see where each one ends up.
